3.text:
For a just identified homoskedastic model $k_{2}=1$

$RB_{N}\simeq k_{2}\mu^{-2}\simeq \mu^{-2}$,  $\mu^{2}= \pi^{2}z'z/\sigma_{v}^{2}$,
and in the weak instrument limit

$kF\stackrel{a}{\sim}\chi^{2}_{k}(\mu^{2})$, $k=1$,

$F\simeq\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})=(Z+\mu)^{2}$, $Z\sim N(0,1)$,

so up to $o_{p}(1)$

$\sqrt F\simeq \mu+Z$.

A $1-\alpha$ one sided lower bound for the concentration parameter on
the normal scale is therefore

$\mu_{L,1-\alpha}\simeq\sqrt F-z_{1-\alpha},\qquad 
\mu_{L,1-\alpha}^{2}\simeq\bigl(\sqrt F-z_{1-\alpha}\bigr)^{2},$

${\rm RB}_{U,1-\alpha}\simeq\mu_{L,1-\alpha}^{-2}
     =\bigl[\sqrt F-z_{1-\alpha}\bigr]^{-2}$.

The $10\%$ Nagar point is $k/\mu_{0}^{2}=0.10$, i.e. with $k=1$

$\mu_{0}^{2}=10$.

${\rm RB}_{U,0.95}<0.10\iff \mu_{L,0.95}^{2}\ge10$ i.e.

$\sqrt F\ge z_{0.95}+\sqrt{10}$,

$F^{*}_{\chi}\simeq\bigl(z_{0.95}+\sqrt{10}\bigr)^{2}$ on the
$F\simeq\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$ scale.  With the one-sided
$z_{0.95}=1.645$

$\sqrt{F^{*}_{\chi}}\simeq1.645+3.162=4.807$,

$F^{*}_{\chi}\simeq4.807^{2}\simeq23.1$,

so that $\mu_{L}^{2}=(\sqrt F-1.645)^{2}\gtrsim10$ and
${\rm RB}_{U,0.95}\simeq\mu_{L}^{-2}<0.10$ for $F\gtrsim23$.
The continuous $95\%$ lower-confidence inversion of the point rule
${\rm RB}\simeq1/F<0.10\iff F>10$ is therefore $F\approx23$ on the
raw non-central $\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$ scale, $23.1$ in round numbers.

On the scale on which the first stage $F$ is normally reported
$\mathbb E[F]=1+\mu^{2}$, $\mu^{2}\simeq F-1$, the inversion is

$\sqrt{F-1}\ge z_{0.95}+\sqrt{10}$,

$F^{*}\simeq1+\bigl(z_{0.95}+\sqrt{10}\bigr)^{2}
      \simeq1+23.1\simeq24.1$,

i.e. the conventionally reported first stage $F$ has to be $\approx24$.
In particular

$\sqrt{23}-1.645=3.15$, $(\sqrt{23}-1.645)^{2}=9.93<10$,

$\sqrt{24}-1.645=3.25$, $(\sqrt{24}-1.645)^{2}=10.6>10$,

so $F=23$ is just below the strict $10\%$ bound and the first integer
on the reported $F-1$ scale which strictly delivers
${\rm RB}_{U,0.95}<0.10$ is $F=24$, the $95\%$ lower confidence
counterpart of the familiar $F>10$, $F-1>10\iff F\approx11$ point Nagar
rule.  With the usual two sided $1.96$ normalisation this is
$(\sqrt{10}+1.96)^{2}\simeq26.2$.  This is the confidence version of the
Stock-Yogo $5\%$ maximal bias point critical value $F_{SY}\approx16.4$
for $10\%$ relative bias.

5.text:
For the just identified homoscedastic case

${\rm RB}_{N}\approx k_{2}\mu^{-2}$ , $k_{2}=1$, $\mu^{2}= \pi^{2}z'z/\sigma_{v}^{2}$,

so the $10\%$ Nagar point is 

$\mu_{0}^{2}=k_{2}/0.10=10$.

In the weak instrument limit

$kF\stackrel{a}{\sim}\chi^{2}_{k}(\mu^{2})$, $k=1$,

$F\approx\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})=(Z+\mu)^{2}$, $Z\sim N(0,1)$,
so up to $o_{p}(1)$

$\sqrt{F}\approx\mu+Z$,

$\mu_{L,1-\alpha}\approx\sqrt{F}-z_{1-\alpha}$,
$\mu_{L,1-\alpha}^{2}\approx\bigl(\sqrt{F}-z_{1-\alpha}\bigr)^{2}$,

${\rm RB}_{U,1-\alpha}\approx\mu_{L,1-\alpha}^{-2}
      =\bigl[\sqrt{F}-z_{1-\alpha}\bigr]^{-2}$ .

${\rm RB}_{U,0.95}<0.10\iff \mu_{L,0.95}^{2}\ge10$ i.e.

$\sqrt{F}\ge z_{0.95}+\sqrt{10}$ on the $F\approx\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$
scale.  With the one-sided $z_{0.95}=1.645$

$\sqrt{F^{*}}\approx1.645+3.162=4.807$,
$F^{*}_{\chi}\approx\bigl(z_{0.95}+\sqrt{10}\bigr)^{2}\approx23.1$,

so that $\mu_{L}^{2}=(\sqrt F-1.645)^{2}\gtrsim10$ and
${\rm RB}_{U,0.95}\approx\mu_{L}^{-2}<0.10$ for $F\gtrsim23.1$.
In particular $\sqrt{23}-1.645=3.15$, $(\sqrt{23}-1.645)^{2}=9.93<10$
and $\sqrt{24}-1.645=3.25$, $(\sqrt{24}-1.645)^{2}=10.6>10$, so $F=24$
is the first integer on the raw $\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$ scale which
strictly delivers the $95\%$ lower bound.

On the scale on which the first-stage $F$ is actually reported,
${\mathbb E}F=1+\mu^{2}$, $\mu^{2}\approx F-1$, the inversion is

$\sqrt{F-1}\ge z_{0.95}+\sqrt{10}$,

$F^{*}\approx1+\bigl(z_{0.95}+\sqrt{10}\bigr)^{2}\approx1+23.1\approx24.1$,

i.e. $F\approx23\!-\!24$ on the raw non-central $\chi^{2}$ normal
inversion and $F\approx24\!-\!25$ on the conventionally reported
$E[F]=1+\mu^{2}$ scale.  With the conventional two-sided $1.96$
normalisation this is $(\sqrt{10}+1.96)^{2}\approx26.2$.

Hence the $95\%$ lower-confidence counterpart of the point Nagar rule
${\rm RB}\approx1/F<0.10\iff F>10$, $F-1>10\iff F\approx11$, is
$F_{\chi}\approx23.1\approx23$ on the latent $\chi^{2}_{1}(\mu^{2})$
scale and $\approx24.1$ on the usual reported first-stage $F$ scale.
Operationally the first integer first-stage $F$ that guarantees
${\rm RB}_{U,0.95}<0.10$ on the $E[F]=1+\mu^{2}$ scale is $F\approx24$,
the $95\%$ confidence version of the familiar Stock–Yogo $F_{SY}\approx
16.4$ point maximal-bias critical value.  The raw normal-inversion
value is $23.1\approx23$.

At this point I think we should be careful not to let the raw \(23.1\) number decide the final vote. It is the correct inversion on the noncentrality/noncentral-\(\chi^2\) scale, but the question asks for the first-stage \(F\)-statistic on the instrument. In the homoskedastic just-identified case, \(kF\dot\sim\chi^2_k(\mu^2)\) with \(k=1\), so the reported first-stage \(F\) is centered at \(E[F]=1+\mu^2\). The Nagar bias is \(RB\approx 1/\mu^2\), so the 10% point is \(\mu^2=10\). A one-sided 95% lower-confidence bound on \(\mu^2\) translates to
\[
\sqrt{F-1}\ge \sqrt{10}+z_{0.95}.
\]
Using \(z_{0.95}=1.645\),
\[
F\ge 1+(\sqrt{10}+1.645)^2
\approx 1+23.11
\approx 24.11.
\]
The nearest whole number is therefore **24**. The \(23.1\) value is the latent noncentrality-scale cutoff, not the conventionally reported first-stage \(F\) cutoff. Even if one stays on the raw scale, the strict “less than 10%” requirement means \(F=23\) gives \((\sqrt{23}-1.645)^2\approx 9.93<10\), while \(F=24\) gives a value above 10. So both operational readings point to **24**, not 23. I would not push the two-sided \(1.96\) route to 26, since the wording is one-sided.
